summary:
Exploring Mars requires more than just knowing where to go. Astronauts and mission planners need access to information about the terrain, environmental conditions, and scientific opportunities around them. While NASA has collected decades of valuable Martian data, much of it is spread across different missions and datasets, making it difficult to turn that information into practical exploration plans.

We developed an interactive Mars exploration platform that brings this data together in one place. Users can explore the Martian surface, view environmental and geological information, discover nearby points of scientific interest, and plan terrain-aware routes for both astronauts and rovers. Our platform also estimates travel times, elevation changes, and terrain difficulty while highlighting potential scientific discoveries along the journey.

By integrating mapping, navigation, and scientific data, our platform helps future Mars explorers make more informed decisions about where to go, how to get there, and what to investigate along the way, supporting safer, more efficient, and scientifically meaningful exploration.
details:
MarsMapper is an interactive Mars exploration platform designed to help future astronauts and mission planners navigate the Martian surface and discover scientifically valuable locations. Our goal was to bring together NASA's planetary data into one accessible tool that supports more informed exploration decisions.

Users can explore Mars through satellite imagery and scientific layers, including surface roughness, thermal inertia, and dust coverage. By selecting a location, they can view elevation and temperature data, discover nearby geological landmarks, and identify hydrous mineral detection that provide evidence of Mars's history of water.

One of our main features is terrain-aware route planning. Using A* path finding and real Martian elevation data, MarsMapper generates routes that account for terrain difficulty rather than simply taking the shortest path. It estimates travel times, elevation changes, and terrain difficulty for both astronauts and rovers, while highlighting scientific points of interest along the journey.

We built MarsMapper using React, Vite, Python, and MySQL. We exported and processed real elevation and temperature data through MOLA (Mars Orbital Laser Altimeter) and JMARS, integrated NASA Mars Trek's mapping services, and incorporated scientific datasets from NASA and OpenSpace. The application is publicly accessible and self-hosted on a team member's server.

What makes MarsMapper unique is its ability to turn scattered scientific datasets into practical exploration insights. By combining mapping, scientific discovery, and navigation, we aim to make future Mars exploration more informed, efficient, and accessible. We also considered terrain resolution and data coverage limitations, so routing and travel estimates are presented as preliminary planning tools rather than mission-certified predictions.

Live Demo: https://nasa.drewbogdan.com/
